practiceQuestions.q: On which date was the Constitution of India finally adopted and enacted by the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constitution of India was adopted, enacted, and given to themselves by the people on November 26, 1949. It came into full force later on January 26, 1950.

practiceQuestions.q: Which article of the Indian Constitution explicitly mentions the date of its commencement, i.e., January 26, 1950?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 394 states that provisions like Articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60, 324, 366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393 shall come into force at once, and the remaining provisions shall come into force on January 26, 1950.

practiceQuestions.q: How many members actually signed the final Constitution of India when it was adopted?
practiceQuestions.sol: Out of the 299 members of the Constituent Assembly after partition, only 284 members were actually present on November 26, 1949, and appended their signatures to the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: Which act was formally repealed by Article 395 of the Indian Constitution upon its commencement?
opts: Government of India Act, 1935 and Indian Independence Act, 1947
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 395 repealed the Government of India Act, 1935, and the Indian Independence Act, 1947, along with any other enactment amending or supplementing them.

practiceQuestions.q: Which major constitutional provision came into force immediately on November 26, 1949, to enable the establishment of the Election Commission?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 324, dealing with the superintendence, direction, and control of elections to be vested in an Election Commission, came into force immediately on November 26, 1949.

practiceQuestions.q: How much time did the Constituent Assembly take to frame the Constitution of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to complete the historic task of drafting and enacting the Constitution of India.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly when the Constitution was finally passed and adopted?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dr. Rajendra Prasad served as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly and presided over its sessions till the adoption of the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: The Preamble to the Constitution of India declares the date of adoption as:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Preamble explicitly states: 'IN OUR CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY this twenty-sixth day of November, 1949, do HEREBY ADOPT, ENACT AND GIVE TO OURSELVES THIS CONSTITUTION.'

practiceQuestions.q: Which national historic event is commemorated by choosing January 26 for the full enforcement of the Constitution?
opts: Purna Swaraj resolution passed at Lahore Session in 1929
practiceQuestions.sol: January 26 was specifically chosen because it was on this day in 1930 that the 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) resolution was celebrated following the Lahore Session of the Congress (Dec 1929).

practiceQuestions.q: Who headed the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was appointed as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee set up on August 29, 1947, and is widely recognized as the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'.

practiceQuestions.q: Why were certain provisions of the Constitution brought into force immediately on November 26, 1949, instead of waiting for January 26, 1950?
opts: To prevent political instability and ensure immediate transition of power from the British Crown
To manage immediate constitutional necessities like citizenship, elections, and provisional parliament without delay
Because the British Parliament demanded an early enforcement of fundamental rights
To coincide with the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi

practiceQuestions.q: What was the immediate legal status of the Constituent Assembly of India immediately after November 26, 1949?
opts: It was dissolved permanently on November 26, 1949.
It was transformed into the Provisional Parliament of India under Article 379.
It functioned exclusively as the Supreme Court until 1952.
It became an advisory body to the British Viceroy.
practiceQuestions.sol: Upon the adoption of the Constitution, the Constituent Assembly ceased to exist as a constituent body and converted itself into the Provisional Parliament of India until the first general elections were held in 1951-52.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Indian Independence Act of 1947 impact the legal sovereignty of the Constituent Assembly?
opts: It subjected all laws passed by the Assembly to the veto of the British Monarch.
It made the Constituent Assembly a fully sovereign body capable of repealing any British act.
It restricted the Assembly only to matters concerning taxation and defense.
It required the prior approval of the Governor-General for drafting any article.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best describes the philosophy underlying the selection of January 26 for the enforcement of the Constitution?
opts: Purely astrological convenience recommended by pandits
Maintaining continuity with the ongoing anti-colonial freedom struggle and historical pledge
International treaty obligations with the United Nations
The financial year cycle followed by the British administration

practiceQuestions.q: Why were articles relating to Citizenship (Articles 5-9) enforced on November 26, 1949, even though the rest of the Constitution awaited January 26, 1950?
opts: To resolve border disputes with Pakistan immediately
To immediately determine who qualified as an Indian citizen amidst the massive partition migration crisis
To grant voting rights in the upcoming British elections
To expel foreigners from civil services instantly

practiceQuestions.q: Consider the dual role played by the Constituent Assembly of India during the drafting phase. What were these two distinct functions?
opts: Drafting the Constitution and acting as a judicial appellate tribunal
Framing the Constitution and enacting ordinary laws for the country (Parliament)
Drafting the Constitution and negotiating treaties with princely states
Managing the army and conducting foreign policy exclusively

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of Article 366 and Article 367, which were brought into force on November 26, 1949?
opts: They dealt with the emergency provisions and financial distribution.
They provided essential definitions and rules of interpretation required for the other active articles.
They outlined the amendment procedure for the Constitution.
They abolished all titles and privy purses of former princes.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the enforcement of Article 60 on November 26, 1949, facilitate the operationalization of the provisional executive?
opts: It prescribed the oath or affirmation to be taken by the President of India.
It laid down the impeachment procedure for the Prime Minister.
It allowed the President to dissolve state legislatures at will.
It transferred supreme command of the armed forces to the British Monarch.

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of the Indian Constitution, what was the primary purpose of transitional provisions like Articles 379 to 391?
opts: To permanently restrict the powers of the Supreme Court
To provide temporary administrative and legislative machinery during the interim period before full constitutional setup
To merge foreign territories into the Indian Union without parliamentary approval
To regulate the taxation policies of British India corporations

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the Constituent Assembly not directly elected on the basis of universal adult franchise?
opts: Because the Cabinet Mission Plan provided for indirect election through provincial assemblies based on restricted franchise.
Because Mahatma Gandhi strictly opposed any form of elections in India.
Because the British Government prohibited conducting elections during World War II.
Because political parties mutually agreed to nominate members without voting.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the adoption of the Constitution:
1. The entire Constitution of India came into force on November 26, 1949.
2. Provisions relating to citizenship, elections, and provisional parliament came into effect immediately on November 26, 1949.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because only specific provisions came into force on November 26, 1949, while the major part of the Constitution came into force on January 26, 1950. Statement 2 is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly:
1. It was constituted in November 1946 under the scheme formulated by the Cabinet Mission Plan.
2. The seats allocated to each British province were decided in proportion to their respective populations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Constituent Assembly was indeed established under the Cabinet Mission Plan in Nov 1946, and seats were allotted based on population roughly in the ratio of one representative to a million people.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the enforcement date of the Constitution:
1. January 26 was chosen as the date of commencement to commemorate the 'Purna Swaraj' declaration of 1930.
2. Article 394 of the Constitution explicitly mentions the articles that came into force on November 26, 1949.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the repeal of British acts:
1. Article 395 of the Indian Constitution formally repealed the Government of India Act, 1935.
2. The Indian Independence Act of 1947 was also repealed concurrently by Article 395.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements about the role of the Constituent Assembly:
1. It functioned solely as a constituent body and never engaged in ordinary law-making before 1950.
2. When the Assembly met as a constituent body, it was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, and when it met as a legislative body, it was chaired by G.V. Mavalankar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the provisions enforced on November 26, 1949:
1. Article 60 (President's Oath) came into force on this date.
2. Article 324 (Election Commission) came into force on this date.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the drafting and enactment process:
1. The Drafting Committee published the first draft of the Constitution in February 1948, inviting public feedback and suggestions.
2. The Constituent Assembly held a total of 11 sessions over nearly 3 years to finalize the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the signing of the final Constitution document:
1. All 389 members of the original Constituent Assembly signed the handwritten Constitution in December 1949.
2. The original copies of the Indian Constitution were handwritten and calligraphed in both English and Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because only 284 members signed the Constitution (due to partition and absences). Statement 2 is correct; it was handcrafted by Prem Behari Narain Raizada (English) and Vasant Krishan Vaidya (Hindi).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the legal continuity ensured during enforcement:
1. The provisions of Article 372 ensured that all pre-constitution laws in force would continue until altered, repealed, or amended by a competent legislature.
2. The transition from British Dominion status to a Sovereign Democratic Republic was finalized on January 26, 1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the Constituent Assembly's representation:
1. The Muslim League boycotted the Constituent Assembly initially, refusing to participate in its sessions.
2. Princely states chose to stay away from the Assembly throughout its existence and never sent representatives.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: Statement 1 is correct (Muslim League boycotted the assembly demanding a separate Pakistan). Statement 2 is incorrect because princely states gradually joined the Constituent Assembly once they realized the inevitability of integration, and their representatives took seats in the Assembly.
